comment: Single source of model constants, shared by the data pipeline (Python) and the app engine (JavaScript). Edit here, never inline.

match_model.comment: slope recalibrated 500 -> 900 on the as-of-then replay of all 46 completed matches (scripts/backtest_model.py): minimum expected calibration error (0.201 -> 0.124), log-loss 0.6988 -> 0.6533, pick accuracy unchanged at 37/46. An interior optimum, not a grid edge: log-loss alone keeps paying flatter models all the way to uninformative, calibration does not. The steeper slope was writing 92% on a semi-final that was lost.

non_knockout_model.comment: Pick rule for pool and stage-2 matches (the ones that can be drawn). Layered on top of match_model, which still produces the probabilities. Knockouts are untouched. 'mode' selects the published rule set: 'validated' is the base plus the parity-convergence draw rule (reference replay 24/36); 'tournament' adds the five switches in tournament_mode (reference replay 34/36). See reference/model_v3/non_knockout_model_v2.py for the author's original.

tournament_mode.comment: The five switches the author derived from the 2026 replay: favourite live-surge, base-draw divergence, head-to-head, ranking-gap band, underdog goal difference. Applied in this order; the gap band runs after head-to-head.

knockout_model.comment: KNOCKOUT_MODEL_V2 — classification, semi-finals and the two medal finals: the matches that cannot be drawn. The model carries no learned constant. It re-derives its weights, its compression and its level rate from the matches already completed on every run, so each match is predicted from everything played before its kickoff. What follows is structure and priors for the opening matches only; scripts/model_knockout.py does the learning.
knockout_model.prior_weight_comment: Used only until min_history matches have been played, then replaced by what the record says. Defence leads because it is what separated sides early in this tournament; the learner is free to disagree later.
knockout_model.knockout_relevance_comment: A knockout result counts three times a pool result when learning for a knockout. The model already treats these rounds as structurally different by compressing the gap; weighing their own evidence higher is the same claim applied to the fit. Structure, not a value tuned against outcomes.
knockout_model.shootout_comment: A shoot-out is scored at exactly one half. The record holds too few of them to claim a side is better at them, and a tilt that cannot be evidenced is a tilt that has been invented.
